pr_title: fix: is_in for bool evaluate has_false incorrectly

issue_context.title: Wrong boolean comparison: Series `.is_in` yields `False is in [False, None] == False` in `0.19.3`
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Reproducible example

```python
# correct
pl.Series([False]).is_in([False])
# shape: (1,)
# Series: '' [bool]
# [
#         true
# ]

# wrong
pl.Series([False]).is_in([False, None])
# shape: (1,)
# Series: '' [bool]
# [
#         false
# ]

```


### Log output

_No response_

### Issue description

When using `.is_in` on a boolean series with a collection that contains `None` the boolean result is wrong. 
Wrapping the collection in `pl.lit()` or `pl.Series()` does not seem to help.

Interestingly, the same **does not** occur for `True`:
```python
pl.Series([True], dtype=pl.Boolean).is_in([True, None])
# shape: (1,)
# Series: '' [bool]
# [
#         true
# ]
```

This issue **exists** in `0.19.3` but **does not exist** in `0.18.7`:
```python
# polars 0.18.7 in old environment
pl.Series([False]).is_in([False, None])
# shape: (1,)
# Series: '' [bool]
# [
#         true
# ]
```


### Expected behavior

`False` is in `[False, None]` should yield `True`
